stem.text: An open-top tray is made from a rectangular sheet of tin 18 centimeters by 48 centimeters by cutting a square of side x from each corner and folding up the sides. The tray can be at most 2 centimeters tall. Find the largest possible volume of the tray, in cubic centimeters.

worked_solution.text: The tray has height x and a base \( 18 - 2 x \) by \( 48 - 2 x \), so its volume is \( V(x) = x\left(18 - 2 x\right)\left(48 - 2 x\right) \).
The cut must be positive, less than half the sheet, and at most 2, so the domain is \( 0 < x \le 2 \).
\( V'(x) = 12 \left(x - 18\right) \left(x - 4\right) \), which is zero at \( x = 4 \) and \( x = 18 \); only \( x = 4 \) lies strictly inside the sheet.
The critical point \( x = 4 \) is beyond the height limit, and \( V'(x) > 0 \) for every x in \( 0 < x \le 2 \), so V is increasing there and is largest at the right endpoint \( x = 2 \).
The largest volume is \( V(2) = 2\left(14\right)\left(44\right) = 1232 \) cubic centimeters.

options.derivation: the height limit left out of the domain, so the critical point x = 4 is used
the side of the cut square, where the maximum occurs, reported instead of the volume
the shorter side of the base at the optimum reported instead of the volume
